---
title: Section wrapper ids
number-sections: true
toc: true
format:
  html: default
  epub: default
  typst:
    keep-typ: true
  asciidoc: default
  docbook:
    output-ext: xml
  pdf:
    keep-tex: true
  beamer:
    output-ext: tex
  context:
    output-ext: tex
_quarto:
  tests:
    html:
      ensureHtmlElements:
        - - 'section#sec-second.level2 > h2#sec-other'
          - 'section#sec-third.level2.myclass'
          - 'nav#TOC a[href="#sec-second"]'
          - 'h2[data-anchor-id="sec-second"]'
          - 'section#explicit > h2#sec-sixth'
          - 'div#nomerge > section#sec-seventh'
        - - 'section#sec-other'
          - 'section#sec-sixth'
    epub:
      ensureEpubFileRegexMatches:
        - path: EPUB/nav.xhtml
          regexes:
            - ['ch001\.xhtml#sec-second', 'ch001\.xhtml#sec-third']
            - ['ch001\.xhtml#sec-other']
    beamer:
      ensureFileRegexMatches:
        - ['\\label\{sec-second\}', '\\label\{sec-third\}', '\\label\{sec-sixth\}']
        - []
    docbook:
      ensureFileRegexMatches:
        - ['xml:id="sec-second"', 'xml:id="sec-third"', 'xml:id="sec-sixth"']
        - []
    context:
      ensureFileRegexMatches:
        - ['reference=\{sec-second\}', 'reference=\{sec-third\}', 'reference=\{sec-sixth\}']
        - []
    asciidoc:
      ensureFileRegexMatches:
        - ['\[\[sec-second\]\]', '\[\[sec-third\]\]', '\[\[sec-sixth\]\]']
        - []
    pdf:
      ensureLatexFileRegexMatches:
        - ['\\section\{Second\}\\label\{sec-second\}', '\\phantomsection\\label\{sec-other\}']
        - ['\\phantomsection\\label\{sec-second\}']
    typst:
      ensureTypstFileRegexMatches:
        - ['= Second(\r\n?|\n)<sec-second>']
        - ['\] <sec-second>']
---

Pandoc 3.13 merges a Div with an id that starts with a heading into the
heading's section, giving the section the Div's id. This document checks
that Quarto keeps the heading id on the section (the crossref target) for
the formats where the merge would otherwise change ids, and leaves pdf and
typst alone because they write both ids.

See @sec-second, @sec-third and @sec-sixth.
